rubric.result: The objective is 'POST /sessions/:id/input writes what the page typed into the session', and every part of it is in the diff. The path is mounted in api-server.ts with the same middleware chain as the other POSTs (Browsers.turnAwayForeign, JsonBody.demandDeclared, JsonBody.reader()); SessionInputRoute.handledBy parses the body, resolves :id through liveSessions.find, and on success calls typeIntoSession.execute(new TypeIntoSessionParams({session, text})), answering 202 {status:'typed', id}. TypeIntoSession.execute hands the text to liveSessions.write, and the already-committed PtyLiveSessions.write ({session,text}) reaches terminal.write(text), so the write has production code behind it end to end. The one thing missing at run time is the collaborator itself: ct-api.ts does not pass typeIntoSession, so this.typeIntoSession! is undefined in the running backend today. That is not a shortfall of this task — ct-api.ts is not in this task's **Files:** and the plan assigns the wiring to Task 10 ('Tasks 4 and 5 mount their routes on ApiServer but nothing hands them their collaborators'), so writing it here would have been an alcance finding instead.

The **TDD:** line names it('the text typed on the page reaches the session') and fixes the assertion: 'a body of {"text":"ls\r"} writes exactly ls\r into that session'. The test in session-input-route.test.ts posts exactly that body ('{"text":"ls\\r"}') to /sessions/session-1/input through a real listening server, and asserts response.status 202, the literal body {status:'typed', id:claude.id} and typeIntoSession.asked toEqual [{session: claude, text: 'ls\r'}] — same input, same expected value, and the expected value is the exact string the plan wrote, with the carriage return preserved rather than trimmed. The controller doubles the use case by construction, which is what conventions/testing.md's layer table prescribes for a controller; the port-level half of the same assertion is pinned in type-into-session.test.ts ('the action hands the port the session and the text'), which asserts liveSessions.asked toEqual [{session: claude, text: 'ls\r'}].

Both Contract blocks were compared symbol by symbol. TypeIntoSessionParams declares readonly session: LiveSession and readonly text: string; TypeIntoSession takes {liveSessions} through the constructor and execute(params: TypeIntoSessionParams): void returns nothing, as the block states. SessionInputOutcome carries exactly the five members with the five literal values ('accepted', 'body-not-a-json-object', 'unknown-field', 'malformed-text', 'session-not-live'), frozen and as const. SessionInputRoute has PATH '/sessions/:id/input', METHOD 'POST', TEXT_FIELD 'text', handledBy(liveSessions, typeIntoSession): RequestHandler and refuseOtherMethods(request, response): void. The prose contract holds too: SessionInputRequest parses and SessionInputRefusal projects in review-plan-route.ts's shape; the one known field is text, non-empty with no control character forbidden (#isWellFormedText is 'typeof given === string && given.length > 0', no trim and no /[^\P{Cc}\n\r\t]/u, which is the declared departure from the imitated route and is what the brief instructs); :id goes through liveSessions.find and null refuses session-not-live with 400; the answer is 202 {"status":"typed","id":"…"}; ApiServer mounts it with JsonBody.demandDeclared and JsonBody.reader(). TEXT_FIELD living on SessionInputRoute (not on the private request model, as ReviewRequest does) is what the Contract block itself names, and SessionInputRequest.KNOWN_FIELDS reads it from there instead of declaring a second copy — the contract wins over the exemplar and conventions/decisions.md forbids the copy, so that call is right. ONE DECLARED DEVIATION, and I rule it correct: the brief says SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES 'gains SessionInputOutcome.BODY_NOT_A_JSON_OBJECT, .UNKNOWN_FIELD and .NOT_LIVE' and the diff adds only NOT_LIVE. Read literally the instruction is impossible: PlanRequestOutcome.BODY_NOT_A_JSON_OBJECT and SessionInputOutcome.BODY_NOT_A_JSON_OBJECT are the same string 'body-not-a-json-object' (same for 'unknown-field'), CODES already declares each once, and Repeats.within returns each repeated code once — so two further literal entries would make the expected array carry 'body-not-a-json-object' twice against a repeated list that carries it once, turning the task's own Verification command 'npm --prefix backend test -- __tests__/infrastructure/refusal-codes.test.ts' red. 'session-not-live' is the only code that newly becomes shared (SessionStreamOutcome plus SessionInputOutcome), and it is exactly what P-9 asks to be declared. This is the case where a sentence of the plan and a control of the plan cannot both be satisfied: declared here, left out of the findings. The companion half of the same sentence, 'RequestVocabularies.codes() gains both new vocabularies', is honoured literally — SessionStreamOutcome and SessionInputOutcome are both spread in.

Walked the table row by row against the diff. The rows this diff bears on: P-1 (LiveSessions is synchronous) — liveSessions.write and TypeIntoSession.execute return void with no promise, and the handler answers synchronously, so the row is implemented with its value; P-9 (an unknown or dead session id is refused with session-not-live, shared on purpose between the stream's and the input's vocabularies and declared as such in refusal-codes.test.ts) — SessionInputOutcome.NOT_LIVE is 'session-not-live' and the declaration is the one line added to SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES; P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session) — no POST /sessions, no delete and no command travels from the browser, the only new endpoint writes text; P-8 (identifiers, test names and every non-product string are English) — every identifier, test name and refusal detail in the diff is English; D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript) — both new modules and all three test files are .ts with erasable syntax only. No row is implemented with a different value, and the remaining rows (D-1 to D-8, D-11 to D-25, P-2, P-4 to P-7) have nothing in this diff that bears on them.

EXEMPLARS. review-plan-route.ts is the named exemplar and the diff plays the same role: same module shape (frozen outcome vocabulary + type, route class with PATH/METHOD/handledBy/refuseOtherMethods, a private request model with accepted/refused/withUnknownFields/isAccepted type predicate/#isFieldMap/from, a Refusal projection over a Projection), same refusal wording pattern ('unknown field: …'), same Answer.refuseAs/Answer.send calls, same 405 with the Allow header. The deliberate departure — no #FORBIDDEN_CONTROL and no .trim() on text — is the brief's instruction and is what the endpoint is for, so it is not a finding. api-server.ts's mount copies the other POSTs line for line. RULES OPENED: conventions/defects.md, style.md, simplicity.md, decisions.md, domain.md, architecture.md, boundaries.md and testing.md (ct's eight, read from the plugin), plus backend/conventions/this-repository.md, which refuses the declared-debt exemption here, and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md on language. DEFECTS.MD, RULE BY RULE. (1) Closed vocabulary instead of loose strings and booleans: satisfied — SessionInputOutcome is a frozen vocabulary with its type, the outcome is never compared as a loose string outside it, and the dispatch is Projection#of, which throws 'no refusal declared for …' for a member nobody mapped instead of falling into a catch-all; there is no boolean standing in for a state and no optional standing in for an absent member. (2) No raw map as the return value of logic: satisfied — logic returns SessionInputRequest, Refusal, LiveSession and TypeIntoSessionParams, all declared types; the only plain objects are the named-argument bag liveSessions.write({session, text}) (the port's own destructured signature, typed, nothing decided by key lookup) and {status:'typed', id} handed to Answer.send, which is the one step before the wire. (3) Two fields that have to agree: no sentinel — the absence of text on a refused request is carried by the type as string | null, not by '' or 0, and SessionInputRequest.isAccepted is a type predicate that narrows to {readonly text: string} so no consumer reads text without the outcome. outcome/fields do travel together the way ReviewRequest's do, which is the shape the Contract block orders ('in the shape review-plan-route.ts uses'); I am declaring that here rather than reporting it, because it is the plan's instruction and the established shape of all seven existing endpoints. (4) Errors named for what happens, not for where: satisfied — no new error type; the codes are malformed-text, unknown-field, body-not-a-json-object and session-not-live, each named for what happened, none for the module that raised it. BOUNDARIES. What comes from outside is validated on entry once: the body is parsed at the door, an unknown key is a rejection rather than a field ignored (Object.keys filtered against KNOWN_FIELDS), entry is by the contract's name (parsed[SessionInputRoute.TEXT_FIELD]), the validation error never leaves the boundary layer, and the refusal code is declared explicitly beside its detail rather than derived from a class name. The use case depends on the port and never on an adapter; dependencies enter through the constructor by name; the domain imports nobody. Layout: the action under application/actions, the controller under infrastructure as <endpoint>-route.ts, one controller per endpoint with its request model and its projections in the same module — architecture.md's 'one controller per endpoint' exactly. DELIVERY. Neither yardstick prescribes a shape of delivery for a new endpoint here, and the change is additive anyway: typeIntoSession enters ApiCollaborators as an optional field, no existing signature or call site is altered, and no caller is left on an old path. CONSIDERED AND NOT REPORTED, so the reading is on record: (a) 'request.params[SessionInputRoute.ID_PARAMETER] as string' is a cast at a boundary, but it is the verbatim line of the sibling session-stream-route.ts committed one commit ago, the value is genuinely validated one line later by find() -> null -> refusal, and a presence check on a parameter the route pattern guarantees would be simplicity.md's unreachable check; (b) the detail 'no live session answers to that id' now exists in two route modules (SessionStreamRoute.#NOT_LIVE_DETAIL is private), which decisions.md's own carve-out treats as each place answering for its own idiom rather than a business rule written twice; (c) LiveSessionMother/LiveSessionsDouble are repeated across the slice's test files, but that repetition was established by the already-committed tasks 1 and 4 and this diff only follows its host. ONE finding, low, is below.

The only pre-existing test file the diff touches is refusal-codes.test.ts, and the diff carries no '-' line in it at all: two imports, two spread lines in RequestVocabularies.codes() and one entry in SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES are added, and the three it(...) bodies are untouched. The one change that widens the guard — declaring SessionInputOutcome.NOT_LIVE as shared on purpose — is asked for by name, both by the task's own text ('SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES gains … .NOT_LIVE') and by closed decision P-9 ('shared on purpose between the stream's and the input's vocabularies and declared as such in refusal-codes.test.ts'), and it is a declaration the guard then enforces exactly rather than a relaxation: an undeclared repeat still fails. No assertion, case or test ended up asserting less.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. Reverting session-input-route.ts and the api-server.ts mount would make every case in session-input-route.test.ts fail (no route -> Failures.nothingMatched answers 404, not 202/400/405), and reverting type-into-session.ts would make type-into-session.test.ts fail to import. The refusals are decided in SessionInputRequest.from and projected by SessionInputRefusal, both production modules; the 202 body is built by the handler; the text that reaches the double is the one JSON.parse produced from the wire, not a constant the test re-declared on the accept side. The doubles double what their names say and nothing more: LiveSessionsDouble only overrides find(), TypeIntoSessionSpy only overrides execute(), and every refusal case also asserts typeIntoSession.asked toEqual [] — the rule that a refusal never reaches a double. The production chain behind the port is real too: TypeIntoSession calls liveSessions.write, and PtyLiveSessions.write reaches terminal.write.

Inside the six declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the two new modules are the Contract blocks; api-server.ts gains only the import, the optional collaborator on ApiCollaborators, the field, the constructor parameter, the assignment and the two mount lines; refusal-codes.test.ts gains only what the guard sentence asks for, including SessionStreamOutcome, which this task's text asks for by name ('RequestVocabularies.codes() gains both new vocabularies') even though task 4 never wired it. Nothing named in '### Out of scope' is touched: the eight existing endpoints keep their paths, bodies, codes and answers untouched; no endpoint that opens or kills a session and no resize was added; no second frame kind. THE PLAN HUNK: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-issue-327-the-session-channel.md is in the diff but it is not an implementer's amendment, and the brief itself proves it — the brief I was given already carries the post-edit text (no 'Current state (refusal-codes.test.ts, lines 20-22)' block, 'an arrow key and a Ctrl-C are what a terminal is typed', 'In refusal-codes.test.ts, RequestVocabularies.codes() gains both new vocabularies…', and the verification comment 'no code shared by accident'), so the edit predates the brief's composition. Read line by line anyway: it retitles Task 10 and gives it an Objective, a **Files:** list and a Call site block for the ct-api.ts wiring, adds the plan document itself to Task 10's **Files:**, marks ct-api.ts as touched by T3 and T10, and reflows Task 5's Contract block. It removes no route from this task's **Files:**, weakens none of this task's **Tests:**, **TDD:** or **Verification:** commands — the only verification edit is a comment's wording — and this task's six declared paths are all still declared.

Seven new tests: six in session-input-route.test.ts and one in type-into-session.test.ts. DETERMINISTIC — no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep and no network beyond loopback to the server the test itself started on port 0; the only path used is join(tmpdir(), 'ct-frontend-never-built'), which is never written and only fails an existsSync. VERIFIES REAL BEHAVIOUR — each route test asserts the status and the literal body of the answer through a real listening server and a real fetch client (never calling the handler as a function), plus what the doubled use case received; none of them would survive reverting the production lines of this diff. ISOLATED — every test builds its own ApiServer, its own LiveSessionsDouble and its own TypeIntoSessionSpy; the one piece of shared mutable state, RunningApi.#started, is spliced and stopped in afterEach, so nothing leaks a listening server into the next test and no test depends on the order of the file. All three properties hold for all seven. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md reference for the finer half and found nothing to pin to them: the doubles are not asserted for their own existence (every assertion pairs them with the real status and body), no test-only method was added to a production class, and the mock setup is not the bulk of any test. Doubling the use case at the controller is what conventions/testing.md's layer table prescribes, so the skill's general 'mocks only if unavoidable' does not bite here. Names say the behaviour at stake ('a lone carriage return is text and reaches the session', 'an empty text is refused with malformed-text'), and the two sides of the text boundary are pinned by two separate tests over the production predicate 'typeof given === string && given.length > 0'.

findings.what: SessionInputRefusal is exported and nothing imports it: the class is used only inside its own module (line 142, and lines 27 and 32 of the handler), and no test or module in backend/ names it. The exemplar's ReviewRefusal is exported because review-plan-route.test.ts imports it for declaredOutcomes(); this one has no such caller, and the Contract block names SessionInputRefusal without asking for it to be exported. conventions/simplicity.md asks the question directly and it has no answer here. Dropping the export keyword would change nothing else.
findings.evidence: 'export class SessionInputRefusal {' — and conventions/simplicity.md: 'A field that crosses a layer, a parameter with a default, a branch for a state, a method made public, an export: each is justified by a caller that exists today and by nothing else. … The question: which call breaks without it? Name it. If none does, it goes.'
